title: Reporting offers, suggestions, orders, intentions, etc.

sections.title: Verb + (object) + to-infinitive clause
sections.content:
When we report offers, suggestions, orders, intentions, promises, requests, etc. we can follow some verbs in the reporting clause with:
a to-infinitive clause
• 'The theatre will be built next to the town hall.' $ ightarrow$ They propose to build the theatre next to the town hall. (not They propose them to build ...)
Also: agree, demand, guarantee, offer, promise, swear, threaten, volunteer
an object + to-infinitive clause
• 'You should take the job, Fran.' $ ightarrow$ She encouraged Fran to take the job.
Also: advise, ask, call on, command, instruct, invite, order, persuade, recommend, remind, request, urge, warn, tell
Compare the use of ask with and without an object before a to-infinitive clause:
• We asked to leave our bags outside the exam room. (= this is something we wanted) and
• They asked us to leave our bags outside the exam room. (= this is something they wanted)

sections.title: Verb + that-clause or verb + to-infinitive clause
sections.content:
After some verbs we can use a that-clause instead of a to-infinitive clause:
• He promised to arrive on time. or He promised that he would arrive on time.
Also: agree, demand, expect, guarantee, hope, propose, request, vow
With a that-clause the person promising, etc. and the person referred to in the reported clause may be different:
• He promised that he wouldn't be late. ('He ...' and '... he ...' may refer to different people)

sections.title: Verbs rarely followed by a to-infinitive clause
sections.content:
After the verbs insist, order, say and suggest we use a that-clause but not a to-infinitive clause:
• There were cheers when he suggested that we went home early. (not ... suggested to go ...)
Advise and order can be used with an object + to-infinitive clause (see A) or a that-clause:
• I advised that she should accept. (or I advised her to accept.; but not I advised to accept ...)

sections.title: Verb + to-infinitive clause (not verb + that-clause)
sections.content:
After some verbs we use a to-infinitive clause but not a that-clause:
• Carolyn intends to return to Dublin after a year in Canada. (not Carolyn intends that she should return ...)
Also: long, offer, refuse, volunteer, want

sections.title: Reporting clause followed by an -ing clause
sections.content:
When we report a suggestion, either what the person reported might do themselves, or what someone else might do, we can use a reporting clause with advise, propose, recommend or suggest followed by an -ing clause rather than a that-clause:
• The lecturer recommended reading a number of books before the exam. (or ... recommended that the students should read ...)

exercises.question: 'If I were you, I'd read the exam questions very carefully.' → He ___ to read the exam questions very carefully.
exercises.hint: Use 'advise' with an object to give a recommendation.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: advised us
Use 'advise' with an object to give a recommendation.

exercises.sentence: He suggested me to try the new Italian restaurant.
exercises.correction: He suggested that I try the new Italian restaurant.
acceptable: He suggested trying the new Italian restaurant
exercises.hint: 'Suggest' cannot be followed by object + to-infinitive. Use 'suggest + -ing' or 'suggest that + subjunctive'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: He suggested trying / suggested that I try
'Suggest' does NOT take the pattern: suggest + someone + to-infinitive. This is a very common error. Correct patterns: (1) suggest + -ing: 'suggested trying'; (2) suggest + that-clause: 'suggested that I try / should try'. Compare: 'recommend' works the same way.

exercises.question: 'Okay, I'll collect Declan from school.' → He ___ to collect Declan from school.
exercises.hint: He expressed willingness or made a promise.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: agreed
After reported speech, 'agree' + to-infinitive reports a willingness or promise ('He agreed to collect Declan'). Compare 'offer', 'promise', 'volunteer' — all followed by to-infinitive in reported speech.

exercises.sentence: She recommended me the new detective novel.
exercises.correction: She recommended the new detective novel to me.
acceptable: recommended the new detective novel to me
exercises.hint: 'Recommend' cannot take a double object like 'give' or 'send'. Use 'recommend X to someone'.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: She recommended the new detective novel to me
'Recommend' does not follow the double-object pattern (recommend someone something). Unlike 'give', 'send', 'show', 'tell' — which can take indirect objects — 'recommend' requires: recommend + direct object + to + person. The same applies to 'suggest', 'describe', 'explain'.

exercises.question: The Health Minister suggested to improve the country's health care. (Replace 'suggested' if incorrect)
exercises.hint: 'Suggest' is not followed by a to-infinitive clause. It takes a that-clause or an -ing form.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: promised
'Suggest' is not followed by a to-infinitive clause. It takes a that-clause or an -ing form. This verb pattern requires a gerund (-ing form) as its object.

exercises.sentence: The officer ordered to the driver to pull over immediately.
exercises.correction: The officer ordered the driver to pull over immediately.
acceptable: ordered the driver to pull over
exercises.hint: 'Order someone to do': no 'to' before the person — direct object only.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: ordered the driver to pull over
'Order' follows the pattern: order + person + to-infinitive (NO 'to' before the person). 'Ordered to the driver' incorrectly adds a preposition. Compare: 'asked her to leave', 'told him to wait', 'invited them to join' — all take a direct object person with no preposition.

exercises.question: She intended that this could be done without raising taxes. (Replace 'intended' if incorrect)
exercises.explanation:
Answer: said
'Intend' is not followed by a that-clause in standard English. Use: 'intend to do something' (to-infinitive) or restructure. The original that-clause requires a different reporting verb like 'say' or 'suggest'.

exercises.question: To avoid the road works, police have advised ___ the motorway at Junction 3.
exercises.hint: Advise can be followed by an -ing clause when there is no object.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: leaving
Advise can be followed by an -ing clause when there is no object. This verb pattern requires a gerund (-ing form) as its object.

exercises.question: Ricardo said the play was very entertaining and he recommended ___ it.
exercises.hint: Recommend can be followed by an -ing clause.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: seeing
Recommend can be followed by an -ing clause. This verb pattern requires a gerund (-ing form) as its object.
